audit.whatIsWrong: diff says FAV but the tone colour is the EVEN yellow and the final rating line reads 'Even matchup'. The page argues two different verdicts.
audit.why: 54.08% over 1067 games — the largest sample in this slice — with difficulty 6/10 is a genuine favoured lane. Nautilus has no sustain and no gap-closer besides Dredge Line.
audit.corrected: Tone moved to the FAV green and the final rating line reworded to 'Favoured matchup'. Difficulty 6/10 and carry threat 7/10 left alone.

audit.why: The audited nautilus side already flipped exactly these three. The page's own whys[0] and whys[3] describe Quinn winning outright, and whys[4] describes Depth Charge as his one kill window — the chart disagreed with its own text.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3 and 4 re-proposed as one atomic group across both layers, with ratings moved to match: 7/10, 7/10, 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the full layer never names a single Nautilus ability except Dredge Line, and the biggest interaction in the matchup is absent — Depth Charge cancels the Behind Enemy Lines channel.
audit.why: Behind Enemy Lines is flagged channel, interruptible by any CC; Depth Charge is a point-and-click knockup plus stun on 120/100/80s. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target, which is exactly what Blinding Assault makes whiff. Riptide slows three times on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Titan's Wrath burns while its shield holds.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge stated as the channel cancel in both phases[4].why and mid. Staggering Blow named as what the blind denies. Dredge Line given 14/13/12/11/10s and Riptide its 7s-to-5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown block named Dredge Line with no number and nothing else.
audit.why: A missed Dredge Line at rank 1 leaves him with no engage for 14 seconds — that is the whole commit window and the number makes the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns for Dredge Line and Riptide, plus the channel warning on your own ultimate.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Nautilus carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 6/10, Nautilus carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Passive-mark AA trades win every short exchange. Identify how Nautilus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Your range and Harrier resets beat a melee whose only gap-closer is Dredge Line. Own the first wave and deny him the push.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Blinding Assault's cooldown drops toward 9s and you out-poke a sustainless tank — shove him in and take plates for free.

edits.before: Behind Enemy Lines exports your lead — roam on every shove. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge is a point-and-click knockup that also cancels Behind Enemy Lines — never channel while his 120s ult is up.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His only engage, 14s at rank 1. Commit once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto — Blinding Assault whiffs it.

edits.before: Vaulting INTO the fight to feel like an assassin — Vault is your spacing reset, not an engage.
edits.after: Riptide slows three times on a 7s cooldown and Titan's Wrath burns you — leave on the first wave.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Dredge Line, 14s: his only engage — dodge it or Vault out. Depth Charge cancels your Behind Enemy Lines channel.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line, 14/13/12/11/10s: his only engage. Dodge it or Vault the moment it lands. - Riptide, 7s down to 5s: the slow that keeps you inside Titan's Wrath. - Your ultimate: a channel — Depth Charge cancels it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are yours — your Q cooldown drops and you out-poke his sustainless tank body, so chunk plates and shove him in. The one stage to respect is 6: his R is a point-and-click knockup that pins you in place, and into E AoE plus the passive root it's a real kill window if his jungler is near, so track the map before you over-extend. Outside that, blind the hook, kite with W's attack/move-speed steroid, and use your own R to roam while he's stuck farming.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours — Blinding Assault's cooldown drops and you out-poke his sustainless tank body, so chunk plates and shove him in. The one stage to respect is 6: Depth Charge is a point-and-click knockup that pins you and cancels a Behind Enemy Lines channel outright, and into Riptide plus the Staggering Blow root it is a real kill window with his jungler near. Outside that, blind the hook, kite with W's steroid, and roam with R while he farms.

notes: Largest sample in the slice (1067 games) and the page was still hedging between FAV and EVEN in three different fields; that is now one answer. The channel-cancel interaction (Depth Charge into Behind Enemy Lines) was completely absent from both layers despite being the reason level 6 is his row.
